newsitem.title: USA: Mercury adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Mercury adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co., the beleagured consumer finance company hit by massive accounting irregularities, said Thursday its board of directors approved a takeover defence plan.
The company adopted the so-called shareholder rights plan, but said it was not aware of any takeover effort.

Mercury said the plan was designed to protect shareholders from what it called "abusive takeover tactics" and from attempts to acquire control of Mercury without offering a fair price to all of the company's shareholders.
Rights plans typically allow existing shareholders to buy additional stock at preferential terms, making it more difficult for a bidder to acquire the company.
On Jan. 29, Mercury said accounting discrepancies were discovered, causing it to restate earnings lower by about $90 million over four years.

Since then, Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars of debt, been served with a search warrant by FBI agents seeking financial records, hired a new chief executive officer, and has been named a defendant in more than half a dozen lawsuits surrounding the misstated earnings.
The company also lost more than $2 billion in market capitalisation when the stock plunged following disclosure of the erroneous financial information.

In recent days, the stock has moved higher in active trading. After falling to as low as $1.50 Jan. 31 from $14.875 before the faulty earnings report was disclosed, Mercury was unchanged Thursday at $3.375.
On Wednesday, Mercury said it was continuing negotiations with lenders for long-term financing.
